inspection.type:
∀ {k t : ℕ} {C : QuarticQuery.Circuit (QuarticQuery.ForrelationCoord k t)} (i : QuarticQuery.Upper.Col t)
  (s : QuarticQuery.Upper.Addr t) {ε : ℝ},
  0 < ε →
    ∃ f,
      (∀ (x : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.Upper.Loc k t C)), 0 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ 1) ∧
        (∀ (x : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.BitLoc (2 * t) (40 * t) C.size (QuarticQuery.ForrelationCoord k t)))
            (e : QuarticQuery.TestIndex (2 * t) (40 * t) C.size),
            QuarticQuery.localTest C (2 * t) (40 * t) x i s e = Bool.false → f x ≤ ε) ∧
          (∀
              (x :
                QuarticQuery.BitInput
                  (QuarticQuery.BitLoc (2 * t) (40 * t) C.size (QuarticQuery.ForrelationCoord k t))),
              (∀ (e : QuarticQuery.TestIndex (2 * t) (40 * t) C.size),
                  QuarticQuery.localTest C (2 * t) (40 * t) x i s e = Bool.true) →
                f x = 1) ∧
            QuarticQuery.Upper.Runs (QuarticQuery.Upper.searchCost t (Fintype.card (QuarticQuery.Upper.Tests t C)) ε)
              fun x b => QuarticQuery.Upper.bern (f x) b

adjudication_findings.claim: Exact-unitary uniform preparations over m and K items need an approximation bridge in a finite-gate library.
adjudication_findings.reason: Unrestricted computation makes this legal, as r1 says. No approximation theorem is needed for this construction: m=4^t needs only Hadamards, and K can be padded to the next power of two with always-passing dummy tests, which changes gamma by at most a factor 2. Adaptive-to-purified bridge stays required.

presentation.body: To verify column $i$, decode and measure a fresh address $s$. Let $A$ prepare a uniform test index and the exact failing-test flag at $(i,s)$, with $K$ tests. Apply the amplification lemma with $\gamma=1/K$ and $\eta=\epsilon$. Reject if a failed test is found; otherwise accept. Output one exactly when some listed candidate is accepted.
presentation.body_plain: To verify column i, decode and measure a fresh address s. Let A prepare a uniform test index and the exact failing-test flag at (i, s), with K tests.
